content.comment_body: My 3-wire proximity sensor operating at 24V always signals a high state. Is this a common issue?
It's difficult to assist without further details. Please provide the sensor manufacturer and model type, or share a link to its datasheet, or upload the datasheet directly.

Measure the sensor’s current output. If it exceeds the input specification of the [product_name] input, then the device will always read a '1' signal. Refer to the 'sensor connection' section on pages 43/44 in the [product_name] manual ([version_no]) for more details.
If your sensor is NPN type, it may constantly register a high state.
Note that the 230V version supports only slow input rates (max 4 Hz). If your sensor operates above this frequency, please review the technical specifications.
A 24V 3-wire proximity sensor cannot be connected to a 230V AC base module.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing difficulties connecting standard 24V 3-wire proximity sensors to the [product_name] base module, with persistent high input readings. The discussion reveals confusion over sensor compatibility, device specifications, and correct input detection. There is a need for clearer documentation and troubleshooting advice regarding connecting sensors to these modules.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward wiring and reliable input detection when connecting general industrial sensors to the [product_name] base module. They look for clear guidelines on compatibility and proper setup procedures.
